description: The court registry code for each court the Caselaw Access Project names (spec section 10.1). engine-output: computed from CAP's case metadata, CourtListener's 2026-09-30 crosswalk of CAP cases to its clusters, and the court registry's names, as each entry's basis says; a court in unmapped has no code, and its decisions are refused unregistered-court; an entry marked review has a code that must be reviewed before any key is minted with it, and its decisions are refused court-under-review until the mark is removed.

bases.crosswalk-90: 90% or more of CourtListener's clusters for the court's cases are on one registered code that fits the court's jurisdiction (stare-builder crates/stare-admin/data/crk/cap_courts.py)
bases.crosswalk-90+name: crosswalk-90, and the code's registry name is the court's name
bases.name: the registry court in the court's jurisdiction whose name is the court's name, letter case and punctuation aside
bases.crosswalk-90-specific: crosswalk-90 once CourtListener's generic courts (uscirct, usdistct) are left out of the count
bases.crosswalk-75: 75% or more of the clusters are on one registered code that fits the court's jurisdiction
bases.name-district: a district of the Court of Appeals of Texas, named in CAP's court name; the district's CourtListener id is an alias of texapp
bases.hand: set by hand from the court's history; the note says why
bases.head-matter: read from the court line in the head matter of sampled CAP case files, with the court's history, as proposed on codexpublicus/exemplar#26 and ruled D154 (2026-10-28); the note says what was read and what a person should still confirm

source.cap: CAP's CasesMetadata.json in each volume of the static.case.law mirror, as of 2026-09-30
source.crosswalk: stare-builder's CourtListener 2026-09-30 export crosswalk (crosswalk.ndjson.gz), one CAP case per cluster
